source.paper: Navigating phase diagram complexity to guide robotic inorganic materials synthesis
source.authors: Chen, Cross, Miara, Cho, Wang, Sun
source.lab: ASTRAL, Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology - America
source.note: 224 robot-run reactions over 35 quaternary oxide/phosphate/borate targets. Phase purity = I_target/(I_target+I_residual) from automated Rietveld refinement. >0.5 high, 0.2-0.5 moderate, <0.2 low. ~10% error bar.
source.why_this_matters: This is EXTERNAL EXPERIMENTAL GROUND TRUTH for route quality. MIRA's validator has never been checked against measured outcomes. The predicted precursors (LiPO3, LiBO2, LiNbO3, KPO3, NaBO2, ...) are largely ABSENT from the Kononova text-mined corpus, which is MIRA's SFT training data - so a model trained on that corpus is unlikely to propose them.

rows.failure_note: BOTH FAILED. Literature uses reducing atmosphere (Ar+H2); air calcination gives wrong V oxidation state (need V3+, air favors V5+).
Glass former - amorphous product, low XRD crystallinity.
Published reaction T is very precise at 790C; rounding to 800C may be too high.
Likely insufficient synthesis temperature; also metastable (39 meV/atom above hull).

rows.MIRA_note: IN MIRA's pass@k HELD-OUT SET, pass@1 = 1.000. Traditional route yields 0.00 phase fraction at 600C, 0.46 at 700C. Predicted route yields 0.52 at 600C, 0.60 at 700C. THE CASE STUDY.

caveats: precursor amounts are placeholder 1.0 (ASTRAL data gives species only, not molar ratios) -- applied identically to both routes, so amount_accuracy specifically carries no real signal here

ranker's temperature_economy/step_economy are ungraded (lit_T/lit_n_ops=None) -- these are already-optimal experimental routes, not model predictions being compared to a literature reference, so that comparison doesn't apply
